endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Establish protocols for escalating and communicating concerns/incidents for resolution to the governance structure

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Establish and maintain procedures for the remediation of issues which trigger incident response processes for the use of a GAI system, and provide stakeholders timelines associated with the remediation plan.

endorsements.title: Developing, purchasing, implementing and monitoring AI tools in radiology: practical considerations. A multi-society statement from the ACR, CAR, ESR, RANZCR & RSNA
endorsements.quote: Institutions should develop a clearly defined escalation and resolution strategy when monitoring detects model failure or performance drift occurs that defines the notification and action plan, and the mode of operation while the model performance is being assessed and the cause of model failure determined.

endorsements.title: Developing, Purchasing, Implementing and Monitoring AI Tools in Radiology: Practical Considerations. A Multi-Society Statement from the ACR, CAR, ESR, RANZCR and RSNA
endorsements.quote: Institutions should develop a clearly defined escalation and resolution strategy when monitoring detects model failure or performance drift occurs that defines the notification and action plan, and the mode of operation while the model performance is being assessed and the cause of model failure determined.

endorsements.title: Operationalizing trustworthy artificial intelligence in clinical and operational workflows
endorsements.quote: Instead, it requires clearly defined ownership, escalation pathways, and authority to intervene when systems underperform or behave unexpectedly.

endorsements.title: Ethical oversight of AI-driven paediatric trials: a proactive, risk-sensitive interim review model
endorsements.quote: Rather than relying on ad hoc negotiation with investigators, predefined deviation thresholds initiate a graduated escalation pathway that may include targeted queries, mandatory corrective action plans, focused audits or on-site visits, temporary recruitment holds, or, in severe cases, suspension of the trial until risks are adequately addressed ( 50 , 51 ).

endorsements.title: Governing Patient-Facing AI-Generated Video in Digital Health: A Risk-and-Ethics Matrix for Deployment, Monitoring, and Change Control
endorsements.quote: Materials that bypass review or breach minimum controls should trigger withholding of institutional dissemination; pause or takedown; incident review; and, where applicable, corrective action under local policy.

commentary.bottom_line: No study has tested whether a documented, tiered AI escalation chain with suspension authority reduces the time harmful tools stay in use, so support rests on seven endorsements from frameworks and commentaries. No study documenting the hazard was supplied either.

perspectives.view: The supplied record contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. The seven endorsements come from two frameworks and five commentaries, and two of the commentaries are the same multi-society radiology statement listed twice. Expert agreement of this kind cannot be graded as evidence of effect under GRADE conventions.

The CHAI playbook frames escalation protocols as a must, and NIST AI 600-1 asks organizations to give stakeholders remediation timelines. Both documents are voluntary frameworks. None of the supplied sources ties escalation chains or suspension authority to a binding federal or state requirement.

The radiology statement asks institutions to define the mode of operation while a failing model is assessed. No supplied study measures how often escalation steps are completed in practice, how long acknowledgment takes, or what staff burden a tiered chain adds. Implementation fidelity therefore remains unknown.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare health systems with and without documented escalation chains and measure time from incident report to acknowledgment, time to suspension of a harmful tool, reporter follow-up rates, and patient harm during the interval. No study documenting how often harmful tools remain active for lack of authority was supplied, so the size of the hazard is also unmeasured.
commentary.underserved_note: No test of the practice exists, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Health systems serving these groups cannot tell from the supplied record whether escalation chains work in their settings or whether reports from these patients reach the escalation process at all.
